description: Calling large language models from the Wolfram Language: one-shot synthesis, templated LLM functions, tool-using agents, chat objects and prompts, configuration of providers and models, and image synthesis.

tools.name: LLMSynthesize
tools.description: Sends a prompt to a large language model and returns the generated text. Prompts may be plain strings, lists of parts, or structured prompt objects. It is the simplest entry point to LLM functionality.
tools.usage:
LLMSynthesize["prompt"]
LLMSynthesize[{part1, part2}]
LLMSynthesize[prompt, LLMEvaluator -> config]

parameters.name: LLMEvaluator
parameters.description: An LLMConfiguration or named evaluator specifying model, provider and parameters.

tools.example: LLMSynthesize["Summarize the Wolfram Language in one sentence."]
tools.notes: Requires a configured LLM service connection and internet access; ServiceConnect sets up provider credentials.

tools.name: LLMFunction
tools.description: Creates a reusable function whose body is a prompt template with slots filled by the arguments. The result behaves like an ordinary Wolfram Language function but is evaluated by an LLM. Use it to turn prompts into composable, parameterized operations.
tools.usage:
LLMFunction["template with `1`"]
LLMFunction[template, params]
LLMFunction[template, LLMEvaluator -> config]
tools.example:
translate = LLMFunction["Translate `1` into `2`. Return only the translation."];
translate["good morning", "Italian"]
tools.notes: Named slots are written as `name` and supplied with an association; an interpreter can be given to parse the result into a typed value.

tools.name: LLMPrompt
tools.description: Retrieves a named prompt from the Wolfram Prompt Repository, such as a persona, a function prompt or a modifier. Prompts can be composed into larger prompts passed to LLMSynthesize or LLMFunction. Use it to reuse tested prompt patterns instead of writing them from scratch.

tools.name: LLMConfiguration
tools.description: Bundles the settings that control an LLM call, including the service provider, model name, temperature, token limits, stop tokens and tools. It is passed as the LLMEvaluator option to other LLM functions. Use it to keep model choice separate from prompt logic.

parameters.name: "Tools"
parameters.description: List of LLMTool objects the model may call.

parameters.name: "MaxTokens"
parameters.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate.

tools.example:
cfg = LLMConfiguration[<|"Temperature" -> 0.2, "MaxTokens" -> 200|>];
LLMSynthesize["List three uses of Fourier transforms.", LLMEvaluator -> cfg]

tools.name: LLMTool
tools.description: Defines a tool that an LLM can invoke, wrapping a Wolfram Language function with a description and typed parameters. Tools let the model perform real computation rather than guessing. Use them to build reliable agents that can compute, search and act.
tools.example:
calc = LLMTool["evaluate", "Numerically evaluate a Wolfram Language expression",
  {"expr" -> "String"}, ToExpression[#expr] &];
LLMSynthesize["What is 17^5?",
  LLMEvaluator -> LLMConfiguration[<|"Tools" -> {calc}|>]]
tools.notes: Built-in tools can be retrieved by name, for example LLMTool["WolframLanguageEvaluator"].

tools.name: LLMToolRequest
tools.description: Represents a request made by a model to call a specific tool with specific arguments. It appears when the tool-calling loop is handled manually rather than automatically. Use it to inspect, validate or intercept tool calls before executing them.
tools.notes: LLMToolResponse carries the result that is returned to the model.

tools.name: LLMToolResponse
tools.description: Represents the result of executing a tool request, in the form that is fed back to the model. It carries both the raw output and its string representation. Use it when implementing a custom tool-calling loop.

tools.name: ChatObject
tools.description: Represents a multi-turn conversation with an LLM, carrying the full message history and configuration. It is returned by ChatEvaluate and can be extended with further turns. Use it when context must persist across several exchanges.

tools.name: ChatEvaluate
tools.description: Sends a message in a conversation and returns an updated ChatObject including the model's reply. It handles tool calls automatically when tools are configured. Use it for stateful chat interactions and agent loops.
tools.usage:
ChatEvaluate["message"]
ChatEvaluate[chat, "message"]
ChatEvaluate[chat, msg, LLMEvaluator -> cfg]

tools.name: LLMResourceFunction
tools.description: Loads a prompt-based function from the Wolfram Prompt Repository and applies it like an ordinary function. It gives access to a library of curated LLM operations. Use it instead of writing common prompts yourself.

tools.name: LLMExampleFunction
tools.description: Builds an LLM-backed function from example input-output pairs rather than from an explicit prompt, performing few-shot learning. The model infers the transformation from the examples. Use it when the task is easier to demonstrate than to describe.
tools.usage:
LLMExampleFunction[{in1 -> out1, in2 -> out2, ...}]
LLMExampleFunction[examples, form]

tools.name: LLMGraph
tools.description: Composes several LLM and ordinary functions into a computation graph whose nodes may run in parallel and feed one another. It is designed for multi-step LLM pipelines such as generate-then-critique. Use it to structure complex prompt workflows.
tools.example:
g = LLMGraph[<|
   "draft" -> LLMFunction["Write one sentence about `topic`."],
   "polish" -> LLMFunction["Improve this sentence: `draft`"]|>,
  "polish"];
g[<|"topic" -> "entropy"|>]

tools.name: ImageSynthesize
tools.description: Generates an image from a text prompt using an external generative image service. Size, count and model can be specified. Use it for illustration and concept visualization inside notebooks.
tools.usage:
ImageSynthesize["prompt"]
ImageSynthesize["prompt", size]
ImageSynthesize[prompt, size, n]
tools.example: ImageSynthesize["a watercolor painting of a lighthouse at dawn", {512, 512}]
tools.notes: Requires a configured image-generation service connection.

tools.name: ServiceConnect
tools.description: Establishes an authenticated connection to an external web service, including LLM providers, and returns a ServiceObject. Credentials are stored securely for reuse across sessions. It is the prerequisite for most external AI and data services.
tools.notes: SystemCredential manages stored keys; avoid hard-coding API keys in shared notebooks.

tools.name: GenerateDocument
tools.description: Produces a complete document from a prompt or specification, with the LLM filling in structured sections and computed content. It can incorporate live Wolfram Language results. Use it for automated reports and templated write-ups.
tools.example: GenerateDocument["a short report on the properties of the normal distribution"]
